title: Effects of new-frame code
statement: Let a word size and compiler size data specify a layout, limits, and stack capacity, and let a state, stack position $q$, and memory satisfy the framed-state conditions. Suppose $q+F+1+F\le Q$. For a list of argument expressions, assume each compiled argument value is already in its corresponding temporary cell, and let the return position $r$ be at most the dispatcher position. After executing the new-frame code, the memory and state satisfy the relation for a new frame whose local variables are the argument values (with missing arguments interpreted as zero), whose ordinary memory is unchanged, and whose stack position is $q+F+1$. The stack cell at index $q+F$ contains $r$, and memory is unchanged outside the writable locations for the new frame.
hypotheses_covered: A framed initial memory and state, including its relation and stack bounds
For each argument index within the list, its temporary cell contains the evaluated argument value with out-of-range arguments interpreted as zero
